MedTrack

What is MedTrack?

  • A private, on-device app for tracking your daily medications
  • Reminders at each dose time, and a simple tap to log it
  • A medication list with supply counts and low-supply warnings
  • A personal aid, not a medical record — it doesn't replace your doctor or pharmacist
  • No account, no server — your data stays on your device
  • Encrypted backups only you can open
01
PART ONE

Every
Day

Seeing your doses and logging them takes seconds.

Today · Home

Your day at a glance

  • A week strip at the top — each day has a ring showing how it went
  • A heading with the date and a progress line, like “3 of 5 taken”
  • Doses grouped by time of day, each with its pill icon and strength
  • Each dose says plainly what happened: Taken 08:00, Skipped, or MissedTakenSkippedMissedNot yet
  • A Low supply badge appears right on the dose when a medication is running out
Today · Calendar

Look back across the month

  • Tap the small arrow under the week to open the whole month
  • A green ring means every dose was taken; amber means a dose was missed
  • Tap any day to see what was taken, skipped or missed
  • Missed is worked out for you — a past dose with no entry counts as missed
  • Past days can be corrected; future days are protected from being ticked early
  • Opening the app on a new day jumps back to today automatically
Logging · taking a dose

One tap per dose, any way you take it

✅
Scheduled

Tap to log

  • Tap the circle once to mark a dose Taken
  • Tap again to change it to Skipped; once more to Undo
  • Supply counts go down automatically when you take a dose
  • Changed your mind? Undo puts the pills back in your supply
➕
As needed (PRN)

The “+” button

  • Tap + on the Today screen, then Add dose
  • Pick the as-needed medication — the dose is logged right now
  • These appear in their own “As needed” section for the day
  • The + menu also lets you add a new medication
Reminders · notifications

Reminders that follow up

  • A reminder arrives at each dose time
  • If you haven't logged the dose, it nudges you again a few minutes later
  • Logging a dose — in the app or from the reminder — stops the nudges
  • Press and hold a reminder to tap Taken or Skipped New in 1.1
  • Choose a reminder sound in Settings and preview each one first
  • Turn reminders off for any one medication on its edit screen
02
PART TWO

Your
Medications

Set up each medication once — then MedTrack does the rest.

Medications · List

All your meds in one place

  • Open the list with the pill-bottle icon at the top of Today
  • Each medication shows its icon, strength, and supply
  • Marked Scheduled (fixed times) or PRN (as needed)
  • A warning triangle shows when supply is low
  • Scheduled meds are ordered by how often you take them, then by time
  • Archive a medication you've stopped — its history stays; or delete it for good
Medications · Add & edit

Make each icon match your pill

  • Enter the name and dose / strength
  • Pick a shape and colour to match the real pill — a quick visual reminderRoundOvalCapsuleTabletTriangleDrop…
  • Set the number to take each time
  • Add dose times on a 24-hour clock, with a Mon–Sun picker for each
  • Or switch on As needed (PRN) for medications with no fixed schedule
  • Reminders can be switched on or off per medication
Supply · stay stocked

Know before you run out

📦
Count

Supply tracking

  • Enter how many you have when you add a medication
  • Each dose taken draws the count down by the number you take
  • The count never drops below zero
  • Taken → Skipped gives the pill back to the count
⚠️
Warn & refill

Low-supply warning

  • Set a warning level for each medication
  • New medications use your default level from Settings
  • A badge appears on Today and the list when you reach it
  • Picked up a refill? Tap Refill and enter the new count
03
PART THREE

Settings
& Data

Make it yours — and keep it safe.

Settings · the gear

Backup, defaults & appearance

  • Back up (export) — saves an encrypted copy you can restore later
  • Restore from a backup — replaces all current data, after a confirmation
  • Default low-supply warning — the level new medications start with
  • Appearance — System, Light or Dark New in 1.1
  • Reminder sound and a plain-language “How reminders work” note
  • A backup nudge: Settings shows your last backup, and a small dot on the gear appears after a month New in 1.1
Privacy & security · by design

Built private from the ground up

📱

On-device only

  • No account, no login, no server
  • No network use — nothing is ever sent anywhere
👤

One person per device

  • No in-app profiles to manage
  • Family members each use their own device
📄

Not a medical record

  • MedTrack is a personal aid
  • It does not replace your doctor, pharmacist or official records
🔒

Encrypted backups

  • Protected by a passphrase only you know
  • Without it, nobody — including us — can open the file
Your data · ownership & recovery

Your data lives only on your device

💾
Keep

Back up regularly

  • Back up creates an encrypted .mtbk file
  • Save or share it wherever you keep important files
  • You choose the passphrase — keep it somewhere safe
  • Uninstalling or erasing the app without a backup loses your data
♻️
Restore

New phone? Restore.

  • Install MedTrack on the new device
  • Open Settings → Restore from a backup
  • Choose your file and enter your passphrase
  • A wrong passphrase or damaged file is refused — nothing is changed
Tips · for getting started

Small habits, steadier routine

🕗
Daily

Build the habit

  • Add each medication with all its dose times up front
  • Log doses as you take them, so the day ring stays accurate
  • Match the icon to your pill — it helps at a glance
  • Allow notifications on first launch so reminders can arrive
🧰
Upkeep

Stay on top of it

  • Enter real supply counts and set a sensible warning level
  • Tap Refill whenever you pick up a new pack
  • Back up after big changes and every month
  • Moving to a new device? Back up first, then restore
